findings.problem: AC-04 requires both provider observation and terminal finalization to remain allowed after proposal/reference expiry or key revocation when current observation authorization passes. TC-04 explicitly proves continued observation under those conditions, but its oracle does not require a found(success) or found(failed(closed_code)) result to be finalized while the proposal/reference or key is expired/revoked. TC-06 proves terminalization generally, but not in combination with expiry or revocation. The current evidence matrix likewise separates observation-only and retry authority without an observable terminal-finalization assertion, so an implementation that permits observation yet incorrectly blocks finalization after expiry/revocation could satisfy the stated tests.
findings.required_change: Extend a required test and evidence oracle to reconcile found(success) and at least representative/all required closed failure outcomes after proposal/reference expiry and key revocation, with current Workspace/resource observation authorization allowed. Require successful Knora terminal finalization, zero provider write/retry, exact public terminal mapping, and proof that expiry/revocation affects new write authority but not finalization of the already-started execution.

findings.problem: The contract requires provider truth to be observed before takeover, while record_execution_observation/finalize_execution require the exact current owner/generation and an unexpired lease. It does not deterministically specify the recovery sequence when the lease is already strictly expired and the provider-first lookup returns a closed success or closed failure. TC-01 covers closed provider outcomes but does not require an expired lease; TC-05 covers stale takeover but not a found terminal provider outcome; TC-07 covers crash recovery without defining this intersection. An implementation therefore has latitude to attempt forbidden stale-owner persistence, incorrectly retry, finalize without a valid lease, or invent a takeover/re-observation sequence that is not contractually tested.
findings.required_change: Specify and test the stale-lease plus found-terminal path. The oracle must define the exact legal sequence consistent with provider-first ordering and generation fencing—for example, observe provider truth without persisting under the expired lease, acquire the stale-execution CAS with one generation winner, then revalidate/re-observe as required under the new current owner/generation before recording/finalizing—with zero provider retry. Whichever sequence is chosen must explicitly prove that no stale owner records/finalizes and that a closed provider outcome cannot be converted into a retry.

findings.problem: DD-07 and the out-of-scope contract require the capability/provider boundary to remain a static typed registry with no dynamic plugins, discovery, runtime provider registration, marketplace, or vendor-specific integration. No required test case or evidence item observes this boundary. A green repository test/Ruff/Compose run alone does not prove that the candidate did not add a dynamic registration/discovery seam or vendor-specific integration, so a material scope violation can pass the acceptance contract.
findings.required_change: Add required observable scope evidence, and preferably a focused test or candidate-diff/architecture oracle, proving that Issue #78 retains the existing static typed capability registry and provider-owned reference boundary, introduces no runtime registration/discovery/plugin entry point, and adds no vendor-specific integration. The evidence must be tied to the exact candidate SHA rather than relying on a generic file-level assertion.
